raw_case_text:
A 41-year-old male was referred for blurred disk margins and possible papilledema from his optometrist. He was visually asymptomatic. He had been seen in a hematology-oncology clinic one month prior for swollen groin lymph nodes that were noted to be reactive, but of unknown etiology. He had not had any previous STDs, genital lesions, penile discharge, or rash.
On exam, visual acuity was 20/25+ OD and 20/20- OS. Ishihara color plates were 11/11 OU. He had a trace afferent pupillary defect OS. Intraocular pressures were 12 OD and 18 OS. He had asymmetric disc edema, greater in the left eye. Optical coherence tomography showed a retinal nerve fiber layer (RNFL) average thickness of 188 microns OS with concentric circumferential elevation and an average RNFL thickness of 118 OD with inferonasal elevation (Figure 1).
Brain MRI and MRV with and without contrast were unremarkable, without mass lesions or venous occlusion. He underwent a lumbar puncture which showed a normal opening pressure of 18 cm H2O, normal protein, and glucose, and 72 white cells/mm3, predominately lymphocytes. Within 2 weeks of presentation, he developed headaches and eye pain, especially when bending over. Repeat examination showed worsening disc edema in the right eye and enlargement of the blind spot on visual field testing. Because his presentation was not consistent with papilledema, orbit MRI was performed, which showed increased optic nerve sheath fluid, especially posterior to the globes (Figure 2) and contrast enhancement of the optic nerve sheaths. Since the clinical and imaging findings appeared consistent with optic perineuritis, he was tested for secondary causes. He tested positive for syphilis with a rapid plasma reagent (RPR), with a titer of 1 : 128. FTA-ABS measured for confirmation was also positive. HIV testing was negative. He was placed on IV Penicillin 3,000,000 Units every 4 hours for 14 days. Repeat testing two weeks after antibiotic treatment showed marked improvement in both his symptoms and the extent of disc edema (Figure 3). Visual field testing also improved after antibiotics, with resolution of the enlarged blind spot (Figure 4).

subjective.chief_complaint: A 41-year-old visually asymptomatic male was referred by his optometrist for evaluation of bilateral blurred optic disc margins, followed within 2 weeks by headache and ocular pain worsened by bending over.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Initially referred for asymptomatic bilateral optic disc edema detected on routine optometric exam, the patient developed headaches and eye pain exacerbated by bending forward within 2 weeks of presentation, accompanied by worsening right optic disc edema and blind spot enlargement.
subjective.past_medical_history: Evaluated in a hematology-oncology clinic 1 month prior for reactive inguinal lymphadenopathy of unknown etiology. Denied any history of sexually transmitted infections, genital ulcers, urethral discharge, or skin rash.
subjective.review_of_systems: Initially asymptomatic; subsequently positive for headache and positional eye pain; negative for vision loss, genital lesions, or rash.

objective.physical_examination: Initial ophthalmic examination showed best-corrected visual acuity of 20/25+ OD and 20/20- OS, Ishihara color vision 11/11 OU, a trace left relative afferent pupillary defect (RAPD), intraocular pressures of 12 mmHg OD and 18 mmHg OS, and asymmetric bilateral optic disc edema (left greater than right initially, with worsening right disc edema and blind spot enlargement at 2 weeks).
objective.routine_investigations: Optical coherence tomography (OCT) showed average retinal nerve fiber layer (RNFL) thickness of 188 µm OS with concentric elevation and 118 µm OD with inferonasal elevation. Syphilis serology was strongly reactive with serum RPR titer 1:128 and positive confirmatory FTA-ABS; HIV serology was negative.
objective.advanced_workup: Brain MRI and MR venography (with and without contrast) were normal without mass or venous sinus thrombosis. Dedicated orbital MRI demonstrated increased fluid within the optic nerve sheaths posteriorly and perineural contrast enhancement of the optic nerve sheaths bilaterally. Lumbar puncture revealed a normal opening pressure of 18 cmH2O, normal CSF protein and glucose, and CSF lymphocytic pleocytosis of 72 WBCs/mm3.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Bilateral syphilitic optic perineuritis / neurosyphilis in an HIV-negative 41-year-old male, confirmed by serum RPR titer 1:128, positive FTA-ABS, CSF lymphocytic pleocytosis (72 cells/mm3) with normal opening pressure (18 cmH2O), and bilateral optic nerve sheath enhancement on orbital MRI. Treated with intravenous aqueous crystalline penicillin G (3,000,000 units every 4 hours for 14 days), resulting in marked resolution of headaches, ocular pain, optic disc edema, and visual field blind spot enlargement within 2 weeks post-treatment.
